_note: Padel IQ framework v0.1 (placeholder). Descriptors marked source=richard came from Richard; source=draft are first guesses for coaches to correct. Self-check quiz questions will live in a separate file and point to skill ids.

axes.name: Movement
axes.short: Position, recovery, moving as a pair

levels.name: Beginner
levels.description: Learning the rules and the court. Rarely gets the ball over the net. Everything before D.

levels.name: D
levels.description: Consistent basics: you return reliably, serve in, and keep a simple rally going.

levels.name: C
levels.description: Controlled shots in friendly games: lobs, bandeja, basic glass play.

levels.name: B
levels.description: Reliable in matches: wins points on purpose, handles pressure.

levels.name: A
levels.description: Complete player: tactics, variety, strong play against good opponents.

levels.name: Pro
levels.description: Professional level. The top benchmark, not an assessment target for most players.

rules._note: Draft rules from design chats. Not final.

levelPass.note: OPEN: all items, or most (placeholder 4 out of 5, no big gaps).

rules.axisLevel: Highest level whose master skills the player passes, worked out per axis.
rules.overallLevel: OPEN: not decided. Simple option: where most axes sit. Shown smaller than the pentagon.
rules.pushingAhead: A skill is 'pushing ahead' when the player's level is below the skill's first master level. It never raises or lowers their level.
rules.unratedSkills: Skills not yet rated are excluded from the calculation. They are not counted as D.
rules.plusLevels: OPEN: 'D+' could mean passed D and working through the C list. No minus levels.

journalPrompts: One thing to try next match?

beginner.text: Learning the serve. Often faults. Just trying to get it in the box.

D.text: In the right box about 7 or 8 out of 10. Soft and floaty. Not deep, no slice, no aiming at the side glass. The goal is just getting it in.

C.text: Usually in, with some depth. Can aim to a side or the body. Less reliable under pressure.

B.text: Reliable first serve with pace or slice. Placement is chosen on purpose and holds up when the score is tight.

A.text: Varies pace, spin and direction to set up the next shot. Targets weaknesses on purpose.

D.text: Avoids lobs or misjudges them. Pushes the ball back rather than hitting through it.

C.text: Gets under most lobs and hits a controlled overhead back, usually deep.
Can hit a bandeja in a friendly game to hold the net. Depth and direction vary.

B.text: Reliable bandeja that keeps opponents back and holds the net, even when rushed.

A.text: Chooses between attacking and defensive bandeja depending on the situation.

B.text: Can use a víbora to add pace and angle when the ball is right for it.

A.text: Chooses víbora versus bandeja on purpose and places it under pressure.

B.text: Can attack a ball coming off the back glass with control.

A.text: Uses the bajada to finish points with placement and power.

beginner.text: Gets some serves back, but often misses or hits it out.

D.text: Gets the ball over the net. Soft and floaty. Backhand is weaker.

C.text: Usually a safe, deep return. Backhand is steadier. Starts choosing direction.

B.text: Reliable return under pressure. Can choose a low, a lob or an attacking return.

A.text: Returns on purpose to win the net and hurts weak serves.

D.text: Can get the lob over the net sometimes, but it's often too low or too short. Only works in an easy rally with plenty of time.

C.text: Usually gets a lob over in a friendly game when there is time. Height and depth are hit or miss. Falls apart when rushed or off the glass.

B.text: Usually lands a deep lob in matches, even when rushed. Pushes opponents back and lets you win the net. Mostly holds when the score is tight.

A.text: Chooses the lob on purpose: side, height, depth. Works from awkward positions and at big points against strong opponents.

D.text: Rarely plays off the glass, and often doesn't succeed when it does.

C.text: Can return most slow or medium balls off the back glass. Struggles with fast or awkward rebounds.

B.text: Reads rebounds early and returns most balls off the back glass with control.

A.text: Uses the glass to buy time and turn defence into attack.

C.text: Can return simple balls off the side glass. Often late on faster ones.

B.text: Reads side-glass angles and returns with control most of the time.

A.text: Handles double-glass balls and awkward angles under pressure.

D.text: Reacts late. Often flat-footed when the ball arrives.

C.text: Usually ready before the opponent hits. Split step is inconsistent.

D.text: Rarely takes the net. Stays at the back after serving and returning. When at the net, volleys are a block that often goes into the net or too high.

C.text: Takes the net when the chance is clear and holds it with steady volleys.

B.text: Wins and holds the net on purpose. Volleys have direction, attacking or defensive as needed.

A.text: Dominates the net. Redirects, finishes and recovers position quickly.

C.text: Sometimes gets back into position after a shot. Often caught out of place.

B.text: Usually recovers to a good position before the next ball.

A.text: Recovers automatically, even after being pulled wide.

C.text: Aware of partner, but often both end up in the same spot or leave gaps.

B.text: Moves forward and back with partner most of the time.

A.text: Moves as one unit and covers the middle without thinking.

D.text: Mostly just returns the ball. Knows the scoring but not yet when to attack or defend.

C.text: Starts to choose between safe and attacking shots. Often tries too much too soon.

B.text: Usually picks the right shot for the situation.

A.text: Chooses shots to set up the next one and targets weaknesses.

C.text: Calls 'mine' or 'leave' sometimes. Middle balls often cause confusion.

B.text: Clear calls and agreed roles, including the middle.

A.text: Adjusts tactics with partner during the match.

B.text: Builds pressure over several shots instead of going for winners too early.

A.text: Changes plan when the opponent adapts.

D.text: Gets frustrated after errors. Focus drops during long rallies.

C.text: Stays calm in relaxed games. Tight scores bring rushed shots.

A.text: Plays the same whether ahead or behind.

C.text: Takes a few points to settle after a mistake.

A.text: Treats errors as information and moves on right away.

D.text: Attention drifts, especially after a long rally or a lost point.

C.text: Focused for most of the match, with dips when tired.

beginner.text: Gets the ball back over the net now and then. The walls are still confusing.
Not sure where to stand yet: back or net, left or right.
